newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY 3YR BONDS MAY BE UNDERSUBSCRIBE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY 3YR BONDS MAY BE UNDERSUBSCRIBE.

text.p: Hungary's three-year government bonds are likely to be undersubscribed at an auction on Thursday as a recent central bank (NBH) suprise rate hike made the offered yield seem too low, dealers said on Monday.

Undersubscription at Hungary's government securities auctions is rare and low demand at the three-year bond's auction would indicate tension between the NBH's and the government's interest rate policies, dealers added.
"The maximum reachable yield at the auction is around the level on the secondary market," said Attila Torok of Postabank Securities. "It is questionable whether all the bonds will be subscribed."
"That's interesting as we have not seen undersubscription for a long time."
The maximum yield at Thursday's auction was set by the Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) at 17.38 percent.

This is 0.65 percent above the average yield at the last three-year bond auction and that is above the usual 0.5 percent spread, but still not enough to create sufficient demand on Thursday, dealers said.
They said three-year government bond yields rose by some 0.7 percent following the NBH's 0.25 percent hike in the interest rate of its six month deposit facility to 21.00 percent two weeks ago.
The NBH move reversed a three-month-long trend of interest rate decline and cooled previous strong expectations for repo rate cuts, with the aim of protecting savings.
The AKK's interest is keeping government security yields low so as to save money for the state budget, dealers said.
Substantial undersubscription at Thursday's auction may compel the NBH and the AKK to discuss their interest rate policies, which seem to be conflicting, dealers said.
"(An undersubscription) will be unpleasant for both the NBH and the AKK," said Zoltan Bereczki of New York Broker.
The AKK will offer 40 billion forint worth of three-year bonds of the 2000/E series on Thursday.
Dealers said insurance companies and investment funds were likely to subscribe for part of that amount as the maturity of the bond was favourable for their securities portfolios.

But speculative buyings are likely to be thin at the auction as three-year yields are at 17.78 percent in the secondary market, where the yields are usually some 0.2 percentage points above auction yields, dealers added.
